title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired Georgia couple lost approximately $800,000 to a cryptocurrency scam that used an AI-generated fake website to display false account balances. The scammers initiated contact through WhatsApp, built initial trust by allowing small successful trades and withdrawals, then deployed a fraudulent interface that showed phantom funds when the victim attempted larger withdrawals. The deception persisted because the fake website mimicked a legitimate trading app convincingly enough that the victim could not distinguish it from the real system.

The failure was in the trading app's lack of out-of-band verification. A system accepting transfers of large sums should have required confirmation through a separate channel, independent of the interface the scammer controlled. No secondary check existed before the funds left the victim's actual account. It is not established whether the legitimate app developer bore responsibility for the scam or whether the fraudsters acted entirely outside the app's systems.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly their entire life savings, approximately $800,000, in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway were contacted by a stranger who encouraged them to invest through a mobile trading app. The scammers built trust by allowing Jerry to make small trades, see modest returns, and successfully withdraw funds initially. However, the fraudsters had created an AI-generated fake website that showed false account balances on the legitimate-looking app, manipulating what Jerry saw on his screen.

The couple discovered the deception when Jerry attempted to make a larger withdrawal and couldn't access the funds, prompting him to call police. Gwinnett County authorities confirmed the trading app was real but the scammers had created a phantom site to deceive investors. The Dunaways are now warning others about these sophisticated tactics while working with police, though investigators say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help the family cover daily expenses as they rebuild their lives.
